title: Mahameghavahana Dynasty
capsule: The Mahameghavahana dynasty ruled Kalinga (modern Odisha) from roughly the mid-second century BCE, emerging after Mauryan decline in the region; its most celebrated king, Kharavela, is attested through the 17-line Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar, which records military campaigns reaching the Ganges in the north and the Kaveri in the south. Kharavela patronized Jainism, repaired temples of multiple sects, and oversaw maritime trade linking Kalinga to Sri Lanka, Burma, and Southeast Asia. The dynasty's attested window in this dataset (c. 170–164 BCE) reflects the narrowly datable portion of Kharavela's reign extrapolated from the inscription; the broader dynasty may have endured into the early centuries CE before Satavahana pressure reduced Kalinga's independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested: the Hathigumpha inscription records campaign destinations but not fixed borders, and the chronology of Kharavela's reign remains disputed among scholars.
